title: Lester Young plays Let the Good Times Roll for his warm-up
summary: While Green warmed up on stage, young Lester Young played along with Let the Good Times Roll, later Symphony Sid's theme.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: And the musicians, I would take it, to start picking up on the tap dancers and what they could do?

Yes. They even started to imitate them. The improvisations that the tap dancers did, in their tap dancing. --like say, for instance, They began to realize that it was jazz (Unintelligible) Lester Young -- the late, great Lester Young. He composed a piece called "Let the Good Times Roll" and I was warming up one day on the stage, you know, just tap dancing. Because We had been riding and sitting down, you know, riding -- your muscles has a tendency to retract, you see. So, I was -- called myself getting limber, you see -- warming up. And he happened to come there, and he was a young musician then, a young tenor player -- saxophonist, and eventually became the president of saxophone, tenor saxophone. He said, "I'm going to warm up. I hope I don't disturb you what you're doing -- your tap dancing. Maybe what I'm playing will go along with what you're going to -- well, let's do some measures." So, he happened to play this melody, "Let the Good Times Roll", and it eventually became the theme song to the Symphony Sid's disk jockey program on the radio. So, I acquired another friend. (Laughter).
Did you dance to the music when he played it?
Yes. It fit it. I was doing measures and tap dancing and he was doing measures and jazz music. But his music was actually "Let the Good Times Roll".
So, you were complimenting each other.

Yes. It was a way of saying keep going, keep on, you know. See, this was all between shows. This was either before the show, you know, because it'd have to be before the show because the shows was appearing with moving pictures then.
And you were developing more, of course.
Because when a good musician plays well, it inspires you to make up new steps and try out new things.
